cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Use the Proper Title
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. At the staff barbecue, introduce me as Director Patel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm introducing everyone by first name. Even the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then give me a separate introduction when I welcome the staff.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner's doing the welcome. You offered to serve burgers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce the burger service: 'Director Patel will serve you.' I'd like them to hear who's making this gesture.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders a titled introduction; A3 claims the welcome and A5 redirects the service introduction after losing that platform, carrying status through pursuit of public respect.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 first-name practice causes A3 separate introduction; B4 owner welcome assignment causes A5 service announcement. A presumed welcome is corrected explicitly.

relationship.evidence: B2 applies an equal naming convention even to the owner and B4 knows the agreed work, giving credible resistance.

heightening.evidence: B4 burger duty causes A5 to make that lower-status service advertise a superior gesture.

specificity.evidence: A1 staff barbecue and B4 volunteered burgers establish the event and role; the absent owner can outrank A without changing A behavior toward B.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 Director Patel will serve you earns the joke from B4 assignment; A3 stock prefix adds unnecessary weight.
